# Every Way To Run Open Source AI Models

![Thumbnail](https://img.youtube.com/vi/vehYE1DfkZg/maxresdefault.jpg)

**Watch:** [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vehYE1DfkZg)

## TL;DR

The video covers every major method for running open-source AI models, organized from easiest to hardest across 4 main categories (local, browser/playground, managed inference APIs, VPS) plus 2 bonus categories (managed cloud, on-device/edge).

## Chapters

### [00:00] Introduction to Open Source AI Models

Defines open-source AI models and their three core benefits: full control over deployment, customizability through fine-tuning, and zero usage cost. Covers popular models as of March 2026.

### [01:44] Category 1: Running Models Locally

Covers local deployment from easy (Ollama desktop app) to medium (calling localhost:11434 from your code) to hard (fine-tuning locally with Unsloth). Discusses hardware requirements including that a MacBook Air M4 with 16GB can run 4B and most 8B models. Also covers Mac mini setups and Cloudflare tunnels for sharing demos.

### [07:45] Category 2: Browser & Hosted Playgrounds

The easiest category for experimenting. Covers arena.ai, Groq.com, Hugging Face Spaces for direct browser access. Also covers Google Colab notebooks with free T4 GPU for education and fine-tuning, noting caveats about session expiry and lack of privacy.

### [10:41] Category 3: Managed Inference APIs

For building software with open-source models without hosting them. Providers like Groq, Together AI, and Fireworks AI host models for you. Just get an API key and call it in ~5 lines of code. Deploy with Railway, Vercel, or Heroku. Best for indie hackers and startups.

### [11:55] Category 4: Virtual Private Servers (VPS)

Rent a VPS (~$5/month from Hetzner or Hostinger), SSH in, install Ollama, and start building. Covers GPU rental via RunPod/Vast.ai for larger models, Docker for running multiple apps, and the popular hybrid approach of local models + VPS-hosted app connected via Tailscale.

### [15:08] Bonus: Managed Cloud Solutions

For startups and enterprise needing automatic scaling. Best for apps with unpredictable high traffic or deploying custom fine-tuned models. Considered hard to very hard workflows.

### [15:58] Bonus: On-Device / Edge AI

Models shipped inside applications so the user's device runs everything. Current examples include Apple Intelligence on iOS and Samsung Gemini Nano on Android. Still niche but predicted to become very popular. Requires small enough models for mobile packaging.

## Key Points

- **[01:01]** Open-source AI models are just as good as closed-source models in 2026 and offer three benefits: full deployment control, customizability, and zero cost.
- **[02:55]** A MacBook Air M4 with 16GB RAM can run any 4B model and most 8B models — hardware requirements are more accessible than most people think.
- **[03:35]** Ollama's local API runs on localhost:11434 — your code calls this endpoint to use local models in your own software.
- **[08:00]** Browser playgrounds (arena.ai, Groq.com) are the easiest way to try open-source models with zero setup, but offer no privacy.
- **[11:00]** Managed inference APIs (Groq, Together AI, Fireworks AI) let you build with open-source models using just an API key and ~5 lines of code.
- **[12:50]** A $5/month VPS from Hetzner or Hostinger is enough to host open-source models for production use.
- **[13:47]** Docker containers let you run multiple models and apps simultaneously on a single VPS without conflicts.
- **[14:03]** The hybrid approach — local models on a Mac mini plus a VPS-hosted app connected via Tailscale — is cheap and secure.

## Highlights

> **"It's a common misconception when people think that it's really hard to run open-source models. That is just not true anymore."** [00:04]
> Opening thesis of the video challenging the myth that open-source models require fancy hardware or coding expertise.

> **"Software goes knock-knock on room 11434. Ollama answers the door and provides the model that you want."** [03:49]
> Colorful explanation of how local model APIs work — your code calls Ollama's default port to access downloaded models.

> **"They're not going to just rent you a GPU for free, right? So be careful about what you're putting into these."** [09:51]
> Warning about using free Colab notebooks — all data goes back to Google and sessions expire without saving your work.

> **"You heard it here first — on-device/edge AI is going to become really popular at some point in the near future."** [16:05]
> Predicting that on-device AI models (like Apple Intelligence, Gemini Nano) will become a major deployment category soon.
